span.label: the cortical basis of auditory backward masking, and whether its unusually long maturation in children is visible in cortical responses
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether standard onset-responsive cortical neurons show backward masking at all, and whether juveniles show more of it than adults
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: backward masking is present in ordinary cortical neurons, arises from both suppressed tone firing and a reduced dynamic range, and is larger in juveniles - mainly through the suppression
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Inhibition evoked by the masker arrives with a shorter latency than excitation, so it can reach back and suppress the response to the tone that preceded it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: In immature cortex the inhibitory response to the masker is larger and slower to decay, so it truncates more of the preceding excitatory tone response and amplifies firing-rate suppression in juveniles.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Juveniles integrate over a longer listening window, which pulls more masker-driven firing into the comparison baseline, shrinking the dynamic range and raising masked thresholds.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Unrefined inhibition in cortex or in presynaptic regions lets an off-frequency noise masker suppress juvenile responses more than adult ones.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: masking arises from a reduction of the signal response together with a higher comparative baseline, which narrows the dynamic range available for detection
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and a shorter latency for inhibition than for excitation lets the later masker suppress the earlier tone, which also explains why a suppressed masker response masks less
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: so the cortical effect may be inherited from earlier regions, with cortex possibly adding to it by reducing rebound excitation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the immature version is attributed to inhibition that decays more slowly and summates more in young neurons
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Recordings were made under anesthesia, which complicates extrapolation to psychophysics.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison with psychophysics only: ANESTHESIA IS ONE CONCERN IN EXTENDING OUR NEURAL RESPONSES TO PSYCHOPHYSICAL COMPARISONS

span.label: MUs → analysis
span.note: AN ANALYST DECISION WITH ITS REASON GIVEN: because multiunits dominated the data set, all single units and multiunits were POOLED for analysis. The composition is 15 SU / 27 MU in adults and 10 SU / 30 MU in juveniles, so the pooling decision is load-bearing for every comparison that follows. No edge type records a choice the analysts made.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE ANALYSIS WINDOW IS A CHOICE, AND THE REASONS ARE GIVEN BEFORE THE RESULT: a brief window isolates backward masking uncontaminated by forward masking, a longer one includes the masker response because behavioral reaction times fall well after masker onset
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE TWO WINDOWS GIVE DIFFERENT NUMBERS: about 18 to 43 dB of threshold shift in the longer window against 13 to 16 dB in the narrow one, with human psychophysics at 20 to 35 dB
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE CORRECT WINDOW CANNOT BE DETERMINED FROM THIS DATA: it would require trial-by-trial mapping of neural activity onto behavioral choice, and IN LIEU OF SUCH DATA the longer window is chosen for two stated reasons
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with both reasons named - detection is measured against the masker alone, and the behavioral reaction time falls well after the masker begins
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A STRENGTH AND A LIMITATION IN ONE SENTENCE: the population neurometric pools every cell, which sits against the rival principle that perception is driven by the most sensitive neurons alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE DIRECTION OF THE OWN BIAS IS SPELLED OUT: because every neuron was tested at its own best frequency, the pooled measure omits the poorly tuned cells a real integrator would receive, and would perform worse if they were included
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE VARIABILITY IS ITSELF A POINT OF CORRESPONDENCE: masked thresholds are quite variable IN CONCURRENCE WITH the psychophysical data, where more measures per participant are needed than for forward masking
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A CORRELATE THAT IS NOT THE CAUSE, SAID PLAINLY: masking correlated with tone-evoked suppression but could occur in its absence, and thus was not the sole driver
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE METHOD IS ALIGNED TO THE LITERATURE IT WILL BE COMPARED WITH: stimuli were delivered monaurally to parallel the majority of psychophysical backward masking studies
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the inclusion rule is set by the perceptual phenomenon rather than by the recording - only units responding reliably to short tones, because backward masking is reliable only for short tones
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A POOLING DECISION JUSTIFIED BY THE COMPOSITION OF THE SAMPLE: single and multi-units were pooled BECAUSE multi-units dominated the data set
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE anesthetic IS JUSTIFIED BY MECHANISM RATHER THAN WAVED AWAY: urethane acts modestly on multiple receptor systems and allows desynchronised cortical activity, unlike ketamine or pentobarbital
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND THE AUTHORS' OWN EARLIER NULL COMPLICATES THE STORY: no age difference in the thresholds of the BEST neurons, suggesting juveniles and adults may not equivalently ACCESS the same sensory information
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with the developmental interpretation flagged as conditional - IF juveniles integrate over a longer window, they would experience larger dynamic range differences
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the locus argued from where the phenomenon is and is not found - backward masking appears in the inferior colliculus but not the auditory nerve or cochlear nucleus, and cannot be peripheral because the signal precedes the masker

span.label: Most auditory cortex neurons required a louder tone to be detected when a noise masker immediately followed the tone, demonstrating backward masking in ordinary onset-responsive cortical cells.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Cortical backward masking arises from two things at once: the masker suppresses the tone-evoked response, and it raises the baseline so that the dynamic range available for detecting the tone shrinks.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Juvenile units showed significantly larger masked threshold shifts than adult units under both analysis windows.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tone-evoked firing was suppressed by the masker more strongly in juveniles than in adults under both analysis windows.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The masker-induced reduction of dynamic range was the same size in juveniles and adults, so the age difference in masking was not driven by dynamic range.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Units that gave no response at all to the noise alone still showed significant masked threshold shifts, so a response to the masker is not required for backward masking.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Population threshold shifts computed over the whole trial (~18-43 dB in adults) matched human psychophysical backward-masking shifts far better than shifts computed over the narrow tone window (~13-16 dB).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In units that did respond to the noise alone, the preceding tone significantly suppressed the noise-evoked firing, i.e. forward masking occurred alongside backward masking in both age groups.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Pooling all units into a population neurometric also produced larger threshold shifts for juveniles than for adults under both windows.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Within the narrow tone window, the loss of dynamic range predicted the masked threshold shift only in juveniles, suggesting juveniles rely more on dynamic range for detection.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The masker caused only a small delay in first-spike latency in both age groups.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: backward masking has a longer maturational trajectory than many other auditory percepts, and its neural correlates are not well described at any developmental stage
